academicTalks.transcript: Today, let's talk about why our planet stays warm enough to support life. The basic idea is that energy from the sun passes through the atmosphere and heats the Earth's surface. Some of that heat tries to escape back into space, but certain gases in the air — what we call greenhouse gases — trap some of that energy and hold it near the surface instead. Explained simply, it works a bit like a blanket: without it, heat would escape too quickly, and the planet would be much colder. Now, if we look higher up, there are noticeable temperature differences between layers of the atmosphere — the lowest layer, where we live, is warmer, while a layer further up is much colder before temperatures rise again even higher. You've probably experienced a similar effect yourself. Think about a car heating in sunlight when it's parked with the windows rolled up — light gets in easily, but the heat has trouble getting back out, so the inside gets hotter and hotter. That's a small, everyday version of the same basic process happening in our atmosphere.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.text: How greenhouse gases keep the planet warm.
How cars are designed to save energy.
How temperature is measured scientifically.
How clouds form in the atmosphere.

questions.explanationZh: 整段講述energy trapped by greenhouse gases讓地球保持溫暖，答案為選項一。其餘選項與講座主旨無關。

questions.stem: According to the lecturer, what happens to heat near the Earth's surface?

options.text: It is reflected away immediately.
Some of it is trapped by greenhouse gases.
It is absorbed only by oceans.
It disappears completely at night.

questions.explanationZh: 講者說greenhouse gases trap some of that energy，答案為選項二。其餘選項未在講座中提及。

questions.stem: Why does the lecturer mention a car parked in sunlight?

options.text: To explain how car engines work.
To compare car design to greenhouse design.
To give an everyday example of trapped heat.
To warn about the dangers of hot cars.

questions.explanationZh: 講者用car heating in sunlight作為everyday example，說明熱能被困住的原理，答案為選項三。其餘選項偏離講座目的。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the layers of the atmosphere?

options.text: They all have the same temperature.
Their temperatures vary from one layer to another.
Only the top layer is ever measured.
They contain no greenhouse gases at all.

questions.explanationZh: 講者提到temperature differences between layers of atmosphere，可推知各層溫度不同，答案為選項二。其餘選項與內容矛盾或無根據。

I'll ask around. By the way, is everything set for the event itself?
Almost — we're just waiting on the city permit, which is required for the event to happen outdoors.
Got it, I hope that comes through soon.

questions.stem: What does the staff member ask the volunteer to do?

options.text: Place collection bins near the door.
Print more sign-up sheets.
Contact the city office directly.

questions.stem: What is still needed before the event can happen?

options.text: More donation bins.
A new volunteer coordinator.
A city permit.

questions.explanationZh: 工作人員提到city permit required for the event，答案為選項三。對話未提及需要更多捐贈箱或新的協調員，選項一、二錯誤。

academicTalks.transcript: Before modern communication, how did people send messages across long distances? For centuries, one common method involved messages carried by riders across long distances, often on horseback. But a single rider couldn't travel forever without rest, so systems developed with relay stations spaced at regular intervals along major routes. A rider would arrive at a station, hand off the message, and a fresh rider with a fresh horse would continue the journey, allowing messages to travel much faster than any one person could manage alone. This system worked well for governments and merchants, but it was often too expensive for ordinary people. That changed over time with postal reform expanding access to letters — lower, standardized rates and more delivery routes meant that everyday citizens, not just the wealthy or powerful, could finally afford to send and receive mail regularly. This shift had a lasting effect on how people stayed connected with family and conducted business across distances.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.text: The history of long-distance message delivery.
The invention of the telephone.
The design of modern postal trucks.
The history of horseback riding as a sport.

questions.explanationZh: 整段講述訊息如何靠騎士與驛站系統跨越長距離傳遞的歷史，答案為選項一。其餘選項與講座主旨無關。

questions.stem: Why were relay stations set up along major routes?

options.text: To sell goods to travelers.
So riders and horses could be exchanged along the way.
To collect taxes from merchants.
To provide lodging for wealthy travelers.

questions.explanationZh: 講者說relay stations讓rider交接給fresh rider與馬匹，答案為選項二。其餘選項未在講座中提及。

questions.stem: According to the talk, who mainly used the message system before postal reform?

options.text: Ordinary citizens.
Farmers only.
Governments and merchants.
Students and teachers.

questions.explanationZh: 講者提到system worked well for governments and merchants，答案為選項三。其餘選項未提及。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the effect of postal reform?

options.text: It made mail delivery slower.
It made sending letters affordable for more people.
It eliminated the need for relay stations.
It was rejected by most governments.

questions.explanationZh: 講者說postal reform expanding access to letters，讓一般民眾也能負擔寄信費用，可推知選項二為正確答案。其餘選項與內容矛盾或無根據。

academicTalks.transcript: Let's think about how a small company sets prices for a new product. It's rarely as simple as picking a number that sounds good. First, the company has to consider production cost — materials, labor, and overhead all need to be covered, or the business loses money on every sale. But cost alone isn't enough; the company also has to think about customer demand. If the price is too high, customers may simply not buy the product, no matter how good it is. So businesses spend real effort balancing production cost against customer demand, trying to find a price that covers expenses while still attracting buyers. There's a third factor, too: competitors influencing pricing decisions over time. If a rival company lowers its prices, the small company may need to respond, or risk losing customers to the cheaper option. Over months and years, this back-and-forth can shift prices considerably, even for a product that hasn't changed at all.

questions.stem: What is the lecturer mainly discussing?

options.text: How small companies decide on prices.
How companies design new products.
How companies train new employees.
How companies advertise on social media.

questions.explanationZh: 整段講述small company如何setting prices，答案為選項一。其餘選項未在講座中討論。

questions.stem: Why can't a company set prices based on cost alone?

options.text: Because materials are always free.
Because customers may not buy if the price is too high.
Because the government sets all prices.
Because competitors never change their prices.

questions.explanationZh: 講者說if price太高，customers may not buy，可推知只看成本訂價並不足夠，答案為選項二。其餘選項與內容矛盾。

questions.stem: According to the talk, what might happen if a rival company lowers its prices?

options.text: The small company must close down.
The small company may need to respond with its own price change.
The small company's costs automatically decrease.
Customer demand disappears completely.

questions.explanationZh: 講者提到competitors影響pricing decisions，rival降價時company may need to respond，答案為選項二。其餘選項未提及。

questions.stem: What does the lecturer mean by 'balancing production cost against customer demand'?

options.text: Ignoring cost to attract more customers.
Setting prices only competitors can match.
Finding a price that covers expenses while still appealing to buyers.
Charging the highest possible price at all times.

questions.explanationZh: 講者解釋balancing的意思是找出covers expenses又能attract buyers的價格，答案為選項三。其餘選項曲解原意。

academicTalks.transcript: Sleep isn't just one long, uniform state — instead, the body cycles through stages during sleep, moving between lighter and deeper phases several times each night. Each stage plays a different role, from physical repair to memory processing. Alongside these stages, the body also releases hormones at different times overnight; for example, certain hormones related to growth and repair peak during the deepest stages, while others involved in regulating hunger and stress shift as morning approaches. Because of this pattern, disrupting sleep — through late-night screen use or irregular schedules — can throw off more than just how rested you feel. The good news is that there are habits that improve sleep quality over time, such as keeping a consistent sleep schedule, limiting caffeine in the afternoon, and creating a dark, quiet sleeping environment. Small, consistent changes like these can make a noticeable difference in how well the body moves through its natural cycles each night.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the talk?

options.text: Sleep involves distinct stages and hormone patterns that habits can improve.
Sleep is a single uniform state throughout the night.
Hormones have no connection to sleep.
Sleep quality cannot be changed by habits.

questions.explanationZh: 整段說明睡眠分階段、伴隨賀爾蒙變化，且good habits可改善睡眠品質，答案為選項一。其餘選項與內容矛盾。

questions.stem: According to the talk, when do certain growth-related hormones peak?

options.text: Right before falling asleep.
During the deepest stages of sleep.
Only in the morning.
They never peak during sleep.

questions.explanationZh: 講者說hormones related to growth peak during the deepest stages，答案為選項二。其餘選項與內容不符。

questions.stem: Why does the lecturer mention late-night screen use?

options.text: To recommend it as a relaxing habit.
As an example of something that can disrupt sleep.
To explain how screens are manufactured.
To describe a stage of sleep.

questions.explanationZh: 講者提到late-night screen use可能disrupting sleep，作為擾亂睡眠的例子，答案為選項二。其餘選項曲解用意。

questions.stem: What does the lecturer suggest to improve sleep quality?

options.text: Sleeping at a different time every day.
Drinking caffeine before bed.
Keeping a consistent sleep schedule.
Using bright lights while sleeping.

questions.explanationZh: 講者建議keeping a consistent sleep schedule等habits能improve sleep quality，答案為選項三。其餘選項與建議相反。
